label: D2 after a2 led rarely to S1 (a2 -> S1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires almost only at D2 (99.8% of mass) when the agent chose a2 and the rare transition took it to S1 (in_action=2, in_state=1); both are observed inputs at D2. Dev F1 0.85, mass recall 0.98; top three activation quartiles are fully covered. Missed activations are weak (lowest quartile, 1.6% of mass), mostly on a2 -> S2 common D2 steps right after a recent a2->S1 rare trial. False positives (~13%) tend to be a2->S1 rare when the agent had just switched to a2 or was mostly choosing a1 (adding prev_action != 1 lifts precision to 0.91, F1 0.86, so it is weaker when a2 is not the established choice). Never fires at GO, essentially never at D1, never on a1 trials (a1->S2 rare does not drive it). Reward is not involved (it is future at D2).

issues: The central claims hold on test. Mass by phase: D2 holds 99.85% (recall 0.993), D1 holds 0.15% and GO holds 0. a1->S2 rare D2 has zero activations (P = R = 0). a1->S1 D2 has precision 0.005. Test F1 0.848 and mass recall 0.984 match the report, and the top three activation quartiles are covered (0.996, 1, 1).

One detail in the explanation is overstated. a2->S2 D2 steps do account for most misses (about 8,700 of 9,839 test misses, which are weak and carry 1.6% of the mass). But only about 2,400 of those come within 2 trials after an a2->S1 rare trial, so 'shortly after a rare a2->S1 trial' covers a minority of them. The rest are a weak, diffuse residual at a2->S2 D2 (precision 0.055).

The false positives cluster in two places. (1) Switch trials (prev_action == 1): 3,807 predicted with precision 0.23, roughly 37% of all false positives. The explanation already says this, and adding prev_action != 1 gives test P 0.907 / F1 0.861. (2) Trials after an unrewarded trial (prev_reward == 0): precision 0.69, against 0.96 when prev_reward == 1. Most of this comes from the switch trials. With prev_action == 2, prev_reward == 0 still gives precision 0.74-0.82. So the unit also scales with the previous reward, an observed variable, which the explanation does not mention. 'Reward plays no part' is only true of the current, future reward.

Neither modulation is a class of steps the predicate wrongly includes. They lower the activation's size within the predicted class, and restricting the predicate costs recall (for example prev_reward == 1 & prev_action != 1 gives P 0.986 but F1 0.72). The simple predicate is still the best compact description.
